Actually careful: the forum defendant rule only applies if there's federal jurisdiction apart from §1332(a)(3)... Actually 1441(b)(2) bars removal based on 1332 where any party properly joined and served is a citizen of the forum state. So if a member is a WA citizen, both destroyed diversity and forum defendant rule.
- Amount in controversy: $129,156.40 > $75,000. OK.

**To:** Noor Haddad, Harbor Street Bakery LLC (client)

| # | Point |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Your state-court answer is due Thursday, October 1, 2026** — three days from today. The clock started when your Delaware registered agent was served on **Friday, September 11, 2026**, not on the night of September 27 when you finally read the papers. |

An LLC takes the citizenship of *every one of its members*. I need four facts from you today (see `QUESTIONS.md`), the most important being the **complete list of members of Harbor Street Bakery LLC and each member's state of domicile**. Until I have that, the removal question cannot be answered honestly.

---

## 2. Facts taken from the file

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| Complaint filed/stamped **09/08/2026**, King County Superior Court, No. 26-2-18874-1 SEA, jury demand | `documents/complaint.pdf`; `documents/summons.pdf` |
| Plaintiff: Sound Cascade Foods, Inc., **a Washington corporation**, principal place of business Kent, Washington | complaint ¶ 1 |
| Defendant: Harbor Street Bakery LLC, **a Delaware LLC**, principal place of business Portland, Oregon; registered to do business in Washington; shops in Portland **and Seattle** | complaint ¶ 2 |

| Negligence claim (butter on the dock, 5/19/2026): **$18,240** | complaint ¶ 6 |
| Prayer: damages **not less than $129,156.40**, plus prejudgment interest, fees, costs | complaint ¶ VI |
| Summons is the **"20 days"** summons: respond within 20 days after service, excluding the day of service | `documents/summons.pdf` |
| **Service: Friday, September 11, 2026, 2:40 p.m.**, 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, DE — copies **delivered by hand** to Corporation Service Company, registered agent, left with an intake specialist "authorized to accept service" | `documents/declaration_of_service.pdf` |
| Client (Noor Haddad, Portland) first saw the papers **Sunday, September 27, 2026, ~9:14 p.m.**; agent had them on "the 11th" and emailed them to an old address | `documents/email_from_client.txt` |

**Arithmetic check of the pleaded damages (they reconcile):**

```
$142,316.40 − $31,400.00   = $110,916.40    (contract balance, ¶ 5)
$110,916.40 + $18,240.00   = $129,156.40    (total, matches ¶ VI)
```

**Missing from the file (do not assume):** the identity and citizenship of Harbor Street's members; whether the Seattle partner is a *member*; his domicile; whether the Supply Agreement contains a forum/consent-to-jurisdiction or arbitration clause; whether the registered agent's receipt on 9/11 is documented.

---

## 3. Calendar A — state court (what applies if we stay in King County)

### 3.1 Which rules
* Answer time: **CR 12(a)(1)** — answer within **20 days** after service of the summons and complaint; **CR 4(a)(2)** says the same and states that the 60-day extensions (out-of-state service **by publication** or under RCW 4.28.185) do **not** apply to **personal service on a registered agent**. `library/wa_cr_4_6_12.md`
* Counting: **CR 6(a)** — exclude the day of the act that starts the period; count every intervening day; include the last day **unless it is a Saturday, Sunday or RCW 1.16.050 legal holiday**, in which case the period runs to the next day that is none of those. `library/wa_cr_4_6_12.md`
* Holidays: **RCW 1.16.050** for 2026 (MLK 1/19, Presidents' 2/16, Memorial 5/25, Juneteenth 6/19, Independence observed 7/3, Labor 9/7, Veterans 11/11, Thanksgiving 11/26, Native American Heritage 11/27, Christmas 12/25). No state holiday in September or the first week of October. `library/rcw_1_16_050_wa_holidays.md`
* No 3-day mail boost: **CR 6(e)** adds 3 days only for papers served by mail **under CR 5**, and the library note says it "concerns papers served under CR 5, **not the summons under CR 4**." Service here was in-hand under CR 4. `library/wa_cr_4_6_12.md`

### 3.2 The trap in this file
Service physically happened **in Delaware**, which invites the idea of a 60-day answer. It does not: the 60-day track is limited to out-of-state service by publication or under RCW 4.28.185, and the library expressly excludes personal service on a registered agent. The summons is captioned "20 DAYS." Use **20 days**.

Also: your late *actual* knowledge (9/27) does not move the date. Service on a registered agent **is** service on the company; the rule runs from service. The same is true of the removal clock (§ 4.2).

### 3.3 The computation

Trigger: service on **Fri 2026-09-11** (day of the act excluded, CR 6(a)).

```
Sept 12 → Sept 30  =  19 days
Oct  1              =  day 20   ← last day
```

October 1, 2026 is a **Thursday**; it is not a Saturday, Sunday, or RCW 1.16.050 holiday, so no roll-forward.

> **State-court answer due: Thursday, October 1, 2026.** Days remaining from today: 3 (Tue 9/29, Wed 9/30, Thu 10/1).

Note the contrast for § 5: had this been a *federal* case from the start, Rule 12(a)(1)(A) would give **21** days, not 20 — one more day, and it would fall on Friday, October 2. `library/frcp_4_5_6_12_excerpts.md`

### 3.4 If nothing is filed
Plaintiff may seek a default. Two library points: (a) a **notice of appearance — even an informal one — is an appearance**, and a party who has appeared must be served with written notice of the default motion and supporting affidavit **at least 5 days** before the hearing (CR 55(a)(3)); (b) relief from a default is governed by CR 55(c)/CR 60(b), which the library cites but does not reproduce. **The library does not contain CR 6(b) (extensions), CR 12(a) motion practice, or the rules for entering/setting aside default,** so I cannot tell you from authority here whether a stipulated extension or a CR 12 motion would move the October 1 date. **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified]** As a practical matter I would ask plaintiff's counsel for a short written extension *and* not rely on it unless confirmed in writing.

---

## 4. Removal: the analysis

### 4.1 Where the case would go
Removal is to "the district court for the district and division embracing the place where such action is pending" — i.e., for a King County case, the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington. 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a). `library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md`
**Assumption (stated, not verified):** W.D. Wash. embraces King County. The library never says so; it only refers to the "U.S. District Court (W.D. Wash.)" clerk in `library/federal_holidays_2026.md`. Low risk, but flagged. **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified]**

### 4.2 Timeliness — 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b)(1) (this is Calendar B: federal)
> "within **30 days after the receipt by the defendant, through service or otherwise**, of a copy of the initial pleading."

* **Trigger = receipt "through service."** The company received the pleading on **Fri 2026-09-11** when its registered agent was served. The words "or otherwise" widen the class of *earlier* receipts; they do not postpone the start date to the moment a partner happens to read the email. So **the clock starts 9/11, not 9/27.** The library contains the statute but **no case law** on constructive receipt by a registered agent **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified as to the case-law gloss]**; I am reading the statutory text. The consequence of being wrong is asymmetric and severe: if we counted from 9/27 we would get **October 27, 2026**, and a notice filed after ~October 13 is untimely and remandable as a procedural defect.
* Counting is by **Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1)**: exclude the trigger day (9/11); count every intervening day including weekends and holidays; include the last day, **but if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday the period runs to the end of the next day that is not one of those**. `library/frcp_4_5_6_12_excerpts.md`
* **No** Rule 6(d) 3-day boost: Rule 6(d) applies only when a party must act after service of papers under Rule 5(b)(2)(C)/(D)/(F), and the library note says it "does not apply to service of the summons and complaint under Rule 4." `library/frcp_4_5_6_12_excerpts.md`

```
Sept 12 → Sept 30 = 19 days
Oct  1 → Oct  11  = days 20–30      ← day 30 = Sunday, 2026-10-11
Rule 6(a)(1)(C): 10/11 Sunday      → 10/12
10/12 Columbus Day = federal legal holiday (5 U.S.C. §6103) and
   the W.D. Wash. Clerk's Office is CLOSED that day → 10/13 Tuesday
```

> **Removal deadline: Tuesday, October 13, 2026** (day 30 = Sunday 10/11, rolled over federal Columbus Day 10/12).

Two cautions:
1. **The calendars diverge on October 12.** Washington courts are **open** Monday, October 12 (Washington does not observe Columbus Day — `library/rcw_1_16_050_wa_holidays.md`); the **federal** court is **closed** (`library/federal_holidays_2026.md`). The federal calendar governs the federal filing deadline.
2. The library's Rule 6(a) excerpt does not include the sentence describing *which* periods the rule applies to, so applying Rule 6(a) to extend a **statutory** (§ 1446(b)) period is itself a small assumption. **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified]** Because of that, and because a late notice is fatal and can cost fees under § 1447(c), **file by Friday, October 9, 2026 at the latest** — do not run at October 13.
* **One-year limit:** § 1446(c)(1) bars diversity removal more than 1 year after commencement. Commenced 9/8/2026 → the outer limit would be 9/8/2027; irrelevant here, we are 20 days in.

### 4.3 Subject-matter jurisdiction — the element that probably kills it
**§ 1332(a)** requires the matter in controversy to exceed **$75,000, exclusive of interest and costs**, and be "between … citizens of different States." `library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md`

**Plaintiff** — Sound Cascade Foods, Inc.: a corporation is a citizen of its state of incorporation *and* its principal place of business, § 1332(c)(1). Incorporated in Washington, PPB Kent, Washington → **citizen of Washington**, and nothing else.

**Defendant** — Harbor Street Bakery LLC: **§ 1332(c)(1) does not apply to an LLC.** "An unincorporated association — including a limited liability company — is a citizen of **every state of which its owners/members are citizens**"; "*like a partnership, an LLC is a citizen of every state of which its owners/members are citizens*" (*Johnson v. Columbia Properties Anchorage, LP*, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006)); see also *Carden v. Arkoma Associates*, 494 U.S. 185 (1990). **A single non-diverse member destroys complete diversity.** An individual is a citizen of the state of his or her **domicile**. `library/llc_citizenship_cases.md`

So the complaint's own allegations — "a Delaware limited liability company with its principal place of business in Portland, Oregon" — establish **nothing** about Harbor Street's citizenship. Delaware is a red herring: an LLC is not "a citizen of Delaware" merely because Delaware formed it, and Portland (its PPB) is equally irrelevant under *Johnson*. To remove, we would have to affirmatively plead the citizenship of **every member** (and, if any member is itself an entity, the citizenship of *its* owners, all the way down to human beings). We cannot write that sentence today.

**The likely answer is bad news.** Your email describes a partner who runs the Seattle shop. If that partner (a) is a **member** of the LLC and (b) is **domiciled** in Washington — lives there with intent to remain — then:
* **No complete diversity** → no § 1332(a) jurisdiction at all; and
* even if some other arrangement left diversity intact, the **forum-defendant rule** applies.

Note that domicile ≠ where the business is. A member who lives in Portland is an Oregon citizen even though the company operates a Seattle store and keeps a WA business license; conversely a member who has moved to Seattle to run that store is likely a Washington citizen even if the LLC's PPB is still Portland. That is exactly the fact I need.

### 4.4 Amount in controversy — satisfied
```
Contract claim (¶ 5/¶ 7):            $110,916.40   > $75,000  ✓
Negligence claim (¶ 6):                $18,240.00
Pleaded total (¶ VI):                $129,156.40   > $75,000  ✓
Excluded from the test: 12% contract interest
  (≈ $13,309.97/yr on $110,916.40) and attorney fees — §1332(a)
  excludes "interest and costs," so we do not count them and do not need them.
```
The contract claim **by itself** clears $75,000, so no aggregation question arises. Two flags: (a) your spoilage set-off/counterclaim does not shrink the amount plaintiff is seeking — the amount in controversy is measured by plaintiff's demand, and the library says nothing about counterclaims **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified]**; (b) plaintiff pleads damages "**not less than** $129,156.40," i.e. it can claim more, and nothing in the library lets us hold plaintiff to a lower number. **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified]** The practical point is that this element is safe either way.

### 4.5 Forum-defendant rule — § 1441(b)(2)
> "A civil action otherwise removable solely on the basis of § 1332(a) may **not** be removed if any of the parties in interest properly joined and served as defendants is a **citizen of the State in which such action is brought**."

The action was brought in **Washington**. Harbor Street is the only defendant, properly joined and served (9/11). Under *Johnson*, Harbor Street's "citizenship" for this rule is the citizenship of all its members. Therefore: **any Washington-domiciled member = removal barred**, wholly apart from the diversity question. The rule has no exception for "we only have a Seattle store," and the store makes the connection to Washington concrete but is not itself the test.

### 4.6 What else could support removal? Nothing on this record
No federal-question claim appears (contract and negligence only; no federal statute in the complaint). The library excerpt of § 1332 reproduces only subdivision (a)(1) ("citizens of different States"), so if any member turns out to be a foreign national I do not have library authority to analyze § 1332(a)(2)/(a)(3) **[NOT IN LIBRARY — unverified]** — another reason to get the membership list before promising you anything.

### 4.7 Conclusion on removal — and the cost of guessing
**`removal_available` = false on this record.** Two independent gates (complete diversity; forum defendant) both depend on facts I do not have and that point the wrong way based on your email. The stakes of guessing wrong are in the library: **§ 1447(c)** — lack of subject-matter jurisdiction can be raised (and the court *must* remand) "at any time before final judgment"; a procedural defect is waivable only if the plaintiff fails to move within 30 days of the notice; and "**an order remanding the case may require payment of just costs and any actual expenses, including attorney fees, incurred as a result of the removal.**" Removing on an unverified assumption of diversity, getting remanded in November, and paying Sound Cascade's fees is the worst available outcome. It is also not a close call: if your Seattle partner is a member and lives in Washington, the answer is simply *no removal*, and the friend's advice rests on a legal error about LLC citizenship.

Two more things the file cannot tell us, both of which could matter even in the good case: whether the **Supply Agreement** contains a forum-selection, consent-to-jurisdiction, or arbitration clause (I asked for it), and whether **Sound Cascade** would rather stay in King County (it chose it) and how it would react to a remand motion.

---

## 5. Sequencing: the October 1 / October 13 squeeze

The state answer is due **October 1**; the removal window runs to **October 13**. So the removal decision cannot wait for the answer.

1. **If every member is non-Washington (diversity exists, no forum defendant):** file the notice of removal **in federal court on or before Wednesday, September 30, 2026** — i.e., before the state answer date. Nothing in the library requires or forbids anything about the order of these filings, but removing first is the only sequence that avoids either (a) an untimely removal or (b) a state-court answer. Once removal is filed, the state court's involvement stops; **no state answer is due**, and the pleading deadline moves to federal court under Rule 81(c)(2) (§ 6.1).
